html:
Istralore (A45)

Region (English ranking partition): Empire of Anbennar (EoA).

1444 starting country: Istralore (A45) Optional formable: Dameria (A58)

In brief: Istralore is an imperial restoration campaign about a loyalist who refuses to let the old dynasty die. Punish Wex, reunite the old allies of the Lilac Wars, revive the Banshees, and ultimately choose whether to restore Dameria or make Istralore a new imperial moon stronger than its former liege.

Story: Very high | Mission-tree length: Long (38 direct missions in the current local script) | Mission-tree update: verified locally for v1.37.5.0; 2025 Final Empire rework | Uniqueness: Very high | Tedium: Medium | Early pressure: Medium | Expansion: High

Identity and history

Istralore (A45) is a half-elf elector duchy in eastern Dameria within the Empire of Anbennar. In 1444 it is ruled by Aucanna I Silistra, has East Damerian as its primary culture, and follows the Regent Court. The local history setup lists Moonhaven and the already fallen Dameria as traditional allies. [Local history script; local localisation]

The country’s origins reach back to the Remnant Fleet’s arrival in Cannor. Istralania Warsinger led the Banshees in the War of the Sorcerer-King; after the war she married the human knight Sideric “the Patient.” Their descendants became the Silistra Silver family and were granted Istralore. The duchy later served Dameria for generations and, after the Empire of Anbennar was founded, became Imperial Marshal and an elector representing the eastern nobility. [Local narrative text; local localisation; Wiki background]

The Lilac Wars destroyed this old order. Istralore stood with Dameria and the Moon Party, only to see Lothane of Wex betray House Silmuna and take the Dove Throne. Defeat did not make the duchy accept the new reality; instead, “loyalty” became a declaration of revenge and inheritance: Dameria might fall, but its imperial ideal must not pass to a usurper. [Local narrative text]

National story and campaign arc

The first half is a political and military reckoning with the legacy of the Lilac Wars. Reclaim the Damerian Hills, support old Moon Party allies, weaken Wex through diplomacy and espionage, and win the electors’ support. Meanwhile, Istralore embraces the Corinite faith and recasts the martial tradition of the Warsinger as a new national identity. [Local missions]

At the campaign midpoint comes the “Imperial Identity” choice. “Dameria Reborn” changes the country to Dameria (A58), moves the capital to Anbenncost, and switches mission trees. “We Will Always Be Warsingers’ Daughters” keeps A45, prevents a later formation of Dameria, and unlocks Istralore’s dedicated second half. That path no longer settles for avenging its former liege: it seeks the Dove Throne, unifies the Empire, and makes the Corinite faith the imperial order. [Local event; local script]

The endgame carries the war beyond the Empire: control Businor to the south, strike at Viakkoc pirates, spread the Corinite faith in Sarhal, and finally launch the Fifth Lilac War against Lorent. The story shifts from “guarding a legacy” toward “defining for ourselves what Anbennar is.” [Local missions; local narrative text]

Core mechanics

Banshees and women’s military reform. Missions revive the elite women’s force descended from Istralania and use parliamentary issues to expand women’s military service, officer education, and labor rights. This is both a military asset and the narrative spine of the duchy’s transition from loyalist old nobility to Corinite reformers. [Local missions; local parliament script]

Imperial electors and the emperor cycle. Istralore is not simply a conquest nation. Many objectives revolve around elector votes, the throne, imperial authority, princes’ manpower, and Imperial Wars; once emperor, its expansion and diplomatic networks reinforce one another. [Local missions]

Old Moon Party allies and “voluntary” accession. Moonhaven, Verne, and Silverforge can be brought into your sphere through long-term relations, joint wars, and political maneuvering. This route demands more diplomatic preparation than outright annexation, but the missions ultimately still require these allies to submit to a unified Empire. [Local missions; local narrative text]

A Corinite state project. Religious war is no backdrop. Convert, lead the Corinite side, reshape the Empire’s religious order, and decide how to treat newer faiths such as Ravelians. Some objectives clearly involve forced conversion and the exclusion of heretics. [Local missions]

Two national endpoints. Restoring Dameria returns to the old dynasty’s name and tradition. Retaining Istralore grants a full sequel that makes the Banshees, women’s reforms, imperial unification, and overseas crusade its own national identity. This choice changes the story that follows; it is not a cosmetic rename. [Local event]

Campaign by phase

Opening: Cultivate Moonhaven, Verne, and other potential allies while preparing to reclaim the Damerian heartland. Fighting inside the Empire brings aggressive expansion, unlawful-territory demands, and elector-relations pressure, but Istralore is not itself a fragile minor.

Preparing the restoration: Rebuild the military industry, revive the Banshees, turn toward Corinite faith, and transform Wex from “the current emperor” into a usurper the Empire can punish together. The mission pacing asks you to manage diplomacy, espionage, and war in parallel.

Identity choice: Forming Dameria switches to Damerian content; retaining Istralore continues the reworked second phase. If you want the country’s most distinctive content, the latter is the complete route.

Imperial endgame: After taking the throne, use Imperial Wars, liberation, and accession to expand Anbennar, then carry the war toward Lorent, Businor, and Sarhal. Late-game expansion is powerful, but the geographic objectives and religious unification add considerable management overhead.

Formable and endgame

Istralore’s campaign is not a fixed requirement to form Dameria. In a central mission event, the player may become Dameria (A58), or inherit Dameria’s political legacy while rejecting its name and continue the dedicated second half as A45. The latter route ends with becoming Emperor of Anbennar, unifying the princes, establishing Corinite authority, and defeating Lorent—not with another Tag change. [Local event; local missions]

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 74/100 | Authoritarianism 60/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 50/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 12/100) | Pluralism 65/100.

The v2.1 values rating is Good (77/100), with a stable trajectory. Women’s education, labor rights, military service, and officer opportunities are clear institutional positives. Restoration wars, religious unification, and imperial expansion primarily affect expansion and restraint; they do not automatically cancel out those reforms.

Recommended for players who enjoy a character-driven restoration, imperial politics, elector diplomacy, women’s military traditions, religious war, and major mid-to-late-game expansion. Not recommended if you dislike HRE-style diplomacy, managing aggressive expansion, event-paced objectives, or simply want a quiet tall campaign.

Community experience

【Community view】A Final Empire-version campaign report rated Istralore 9/10 and praised the story and imperial gameplay, while warning that aggressive expansion, unlawful-territory demands, elector votes, and governing capacity can compound. The report used Very Easy difficulty, so its difficulty conclusion should not be generalized to normal difficulty.

【Community view】A separate “easy countries” discussion grouped Istralore with Verne as a suitable way to learn the revised Empire system. Taken together, these suggest limited survival pressure; the real challenge is diplomacy, expansion within the Empire, and mission pacing—not simply surviving the neighbors.

Evidence limits

This article covers the local base Mod and localisation for v1.37.5.0, checked 2026-09-16. Tag, Chinese name, 38 direct missions, 1444 identity, the branch to form Dameria or retain A45, and the core mechanics are grounded in current local files.

The offline Wiki was checked for Duchy of Istralore (page_id=644, revision_id=31323), Istralania Warsinger (1450/27155), and Aucanna Silistra (4763/28650). These provide background on the Remnant Fleet, Banshees, Silistra family, and reconstruction around 1444. The country page spells the founder’s name “Istralara,” unlike the character page and local text; this article follows the latter’s “Istralania.” Full references and limits are in the evidence record.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Istralore (A45) — Istralorian Ideas

Set ID: A45_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = A45 #Istralore
    }

Istralorian Traditions

  • Leader land shock: +1 (leader_land_shock; raw value 1).

  • Land force limit modifier: +20% (land_forcelimit_modifier; raw value 0.2).

1. Marshals of the Empire

With the end of the Wars of Rule in the late 13th century came Istralore’s ascension as Marshal of the Imperial Army and Elector of the Empire. Despite holding such a powerful position, its dukes and duchesses have (almost) never attempted to further their own interests and have instead sternly held fast to their duties.

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

2. For The Fallen Moon

“My son, my blood, my joy, I speak not as your mother but as your Duchess. The world is unjust. Our true liege lies dead, murdered by a traitor. A traitor who sits upon the Dove Throne even now.

Even though we fought for what was right, Istralore lost both the battle and the war. I’ve failed my charge in too many ways to count. But, my fight isn’t over. Not til my last breath. Wex must be chastened. Lothane brought to account. Dameria avenged.

This is the duty and burden of Istralore. It is mine to bear. And when I’m gone it will be yours. Do you understand?”

“Yes, mothe- Duchess.”

  • Duchess Aucanna I to the future Duke Aucan III

  • War exhaustion: -0.03 (war_exhaustion; raw value -0.03).

3. Istralari Banshees

Istralania Warsinger, founder and namesake of Istralore, was once known simply as Istralania ta Estadh. Usually a reserved and stoic woman, upon the battlefield, Istralania’s blood-curdling cries struck awe and terror in the minions of the Sorcerer-King Nichmer as she slew them by the hundreds. Over the course of the war, others would echo the elf’s battle cries, becoming her “banshees” and striking fear through the Black Legions of Castanor.

In the aftermath of war, Istralania’s Banshees formalized into an elite all-women unit. Forming the core of the Istralari army, the unit saw service through the century long Lilac Wars, Corinite Wars, Camir’s Conquest, and beyond.

  • Infantry combat ability: +15% (infantry_power; raw value 0.15).

4. The Sword of the Accord

“Damnable fools, those Istralorians are. They’d rather plunge the entire Empire into war for the usurper Corin than heed their Emperor!“ - Emperor Galien I síl na Trisfer

With the revelation of Castellos’ death, the Regent Court began its plunge into chaos and final fragmentation. As the question of which god would succeed Castellos echoed through Cannor, a resounding response sounded out from Istralore - the Goddess of War Corin. Boldly defying the eleventh and final Pantheonic Council, the adoption of the Corinite faith solidified Istralore’s place as the frontline of future Corinite Accord within Anbennar.

  • Missionary strength: +2% (global_missionary_strength; raw value 0.02).

  • Yearly Corinite Paragonhood decay: raw value 0.1 (unit unverified) (yearly_karma_decay; raw value 0.1).

5. Heirs of the Estádha

Almost every Istralani noble can trace their lineage back to an elf aboard the Migrant Ship Estádha. Captained by Istralania Warsinger, she and the ship’s inhabitants were the first to accept Munas Moonsinger's bold claims and follow the moon towards a new home. Their show of courage convinced the rest of the Remnant Fleet to follow Munas as well, bringing an end to the thousand-year Great Wander. Today, centuries later, just as the blood of the Estádha still courses within Istralore, so too does that same courage and conviction to chart a course into the unknown.

  • Naval Morale: +10% (naval_morale; raw value 0.1).

6. The Dalemines

Across the rolling hills of the Damerian Dales, the forested landscape is dotted by mines churning out ores of all sorts. But, this was not always so. At first, simple holes were dug by the ancient Damerid tribes to acquire the easiest deposits. Armed with iron might, these humble tribes rose to found the Damerian Republic, marking the start of a storied history. In the centuries after, as the Republic became Kingdom and later Grand Duchy, true mines sprung into being giving name to the Dalemines. With the final fall of Dameria, Istralore now stands as heir to the mines and its legacy.

  • global_regiment_cost: -10% (global_regiment_cost; raw value -0.1).

7. Sealion Proclamation

The First Great Damesear Raid was a disaster that stopped just shy of catastrophe. The Damish Temple of Moon Isle had been defiled by the demon worshipping gnolls of Viakkoc. Anbenncóst smoldered in the embers of demonflame. Thousands were dead, thousands more taken as slaves.

It was in this backdrop that Ricain Silistra, adventurer and future Duke of Istralore, rode across the countryside. Still covered with soot, sweat, and blood from fending off raiders, he swept from town to town waving the banner of Istralore’s venerable Sealion and calling upon every righteous soul to follow him. By the time of his arrival in Duchy’s capital of Cilseinn, thousands stood behind him. Planting the now tattered banner behind him, he proclaimed a new crusade -- in Corin’s name.

  • Naval tradition: +1 (navy_tradition; raw value 1).

Istralorian Ambition

  • Manpower from true faith provinces: +15% (manpower_in_true_faith_provinces; raw value 0.15).

Dameria (A58) — Damerian Ideas

Set ID: A58_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = A58 #Dameria
    }

Damerian Traditions

  • Chance of a new heir: +50% (heir_chance; raw value 0.5).

  • Improve relations: +30% (improve_relation_modifier; raw value 0.3).

1. Imperial Sovereignty

The Silmunas have sat on the imperial throne of Anbennar for much of its history, and by the graces of the gods an Anbennar without a Silmuna is no Anbennar at all.

  • Imperial authority growth modifier: +0.1 (imperial_authority; raw value 0.1).

  • Diplomatic relations: +1 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 1).

2. Wooden Wall of Damesear

Dameria's position as lord of the Damesear has allowed it to become a great power across all of Cannor, but to protect the isle from any would-be invaders it must be protected by a wooden wall: the finest ships in the Dameshead.

  • Galley construction cost: -15% (galley_cost; raw value -0.15).

  • Galley Combat Ability: +20% (galley_power; raw value 0.20).

3. Damerian Court Conduct

Most royal courts in history were modeled of the Damerian Court during the Interregnum where we established properly court conduct, etiquette and ceremony.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +200% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 2).

4. Silmuna School of the Arts

Founded in 1024, the Silmuna School is one of the most prestigious institutions of magic, sciences and arts in all of Cannor.

  • Idea cost: -10% (idea_cost; raw value -0.1).

5. Damerian Adventurer Companies

Dameria won its wars due to their adventurer irregulars, whom often found a home in Anbenncóst or as newly found nobility under the kingdom.

  • Mercenary Cost: -15% (mercenary_cost; raw value -0.15).

  • Mercenary Discipline: +10% (mercenary_discipline; raw value 0.1).

6. Legacy of the Damerian Republic

Before the Grand Duchy was the Kingdom, and before the Kingdom was the Republic: the ancient force that civilized all of Cannor and made it what it is today.

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

7. Anbenncóst, the City of the World's Desire

At the highest hill of Anbenncóst sits the Imperial Palace, formerly the Damerian Palace. Though no doubt, the strength of Dameria lies not in its diplomacy, nor its traditions, but the people of Anbenncóst that form the foundation of all things right.

  • Domestic trade power: +20% (global_own_trade_power; raw value 0.2).

Damerian Ambition

  • Army morale: +20% (land_morale; raw value 0.2).
